extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, and third-party requesters/practitioners handling inter partes reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules from the MPEP governing excess claim fees, timing, content, service, and examiner handling of papers and withdrawals in inter partes reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees applicability in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess claims fees as specified in 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(2) (and 37 CFR 1.20(c)) apply to excess claims proposed to be added to a patent by their presentation during a reexamination proceeding on or after December 8, 2004.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are due “on filing or on presentation at any other time” of an independent claim in excess of three or of a claim (whether independent or dependent) in excess of twenty. No excess claims fee was due for claims presented during reexamination before December 8, 2004. If a reexamination was commenced prior to December 8, 2004, excess claims fees are due for any amendment filed on or after December 8, 2004. If the amendment only revises existing claims and does not provide any new claim, no claim fee is due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent excess claims fee calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee designated in 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) (independent claims fee) must be paid for each independent claim in excess of three and also in excess of the number of independent claims in the patent being reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amendment must increase the number of independent claims to be more than both of these limits in order for the independent excess claims fee to apply. Example: if patent has six independent claims, adding a seventh independent claim (after appropriate cancellations/additions) can trigger the 1.20(c)(3) fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total excess claims fee calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee designated in 37 CFR 1.20(c)(4) (total claims fee) must be paid for each claim (independent or dependent) in excess of twenty and also in excess of the number of claims in the patent being reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amendment must increase the total number of claims to be more than both of these limits in order for the total excess claims fee to apply. Example: if patent has thirty total claims, adding a thirty-first claim will trigger the 1.20(c)(4) fee unless cancellations reduce the count below the threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples illustrating excess claims fee application
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete scenarios showing when excess independent and/or total claims fees are due given cancellations and additions of claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: (A) cancel ten claims (two independent) and add ten claims (two independent) — no excess fee; (B) cancel ten (two independent), add ten (three independent) — independent excess fee due for seventh independent claim; (C) cancel ten (two independent), add eleven (two independent) — total excess fee due for thirty-first claim; (D) cancel ten (two independent), add eleven (three independent) — both independent and total excess fees due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee deficiency notification and correction
rubrics_metrics.description: If excess claims fees required by 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) are not paid with presentation of excess claims, a Notice of Defective Paper (PTOL-2069) will be issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTOL-2069 sets a one-month time period to correct the defect; an extension may be requested under 37 CFR 1.956. If unpaid within the response period, prosecution of the reexamination proceeding will be terminated under 37 CFR 1.957(b) or limited under 37 CFR 1.957(c) to effect the “abandonment” set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(c)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party comments timing (37 CFR 1.947)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each time the patent owner files a response to an Office action on the merits, a third party requester may once file written comments within 30 days from the date of service of the patent owner’s response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time for submitting comments may not be extended. For filing purposes, comments are considered received as of the deposit date specified in the certificate under 37 CFR 1.8. The Office receipt date of the patent owner’s response does not affect the requester's 30-day clock.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party comments content and structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Third party requester comments shall be limited to issues raised by the Office action or the patent owner’s response and should specify point/issue, the page where point is recited, and present discussion and argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comments should (1) set forth the point or issue, (2) state the page of the Office action and/or patent owner’s response where the point/issue is recited, and (3) present discussion/argument. If not done exactly, comments need not be held defective if examiner can ascertain that all comments are directed to issues covered by the Office action/patent owner response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for submitting new prior art with comments (37 CFR 1.948(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: After the inter partes reexamination order, a third party requester may cite additional prior art as part of a comments submission only if it is limited to prior art that: (1) is necessary to rebut an examiner finding of fact, (2) is necessary to rebut a patent owner response, or (3) for the first time became known or available to the requester after filing the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior art submitted under (a)(3) must be accompanied by a statement when the art first became known/available and include a discussion of the pertinency of each reference to the patentability of at least one claim. Any newly proposed rejection standing on such art must comply with MPEP §2617, including required discussion of pertinency and explanation pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 311 of how the art is applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on substituting new art to replace art of record
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement in an Office action that a claimed feature is not shown by the prior art of record does NOT permit the requester to cite new art to replace the art originally advanced by the requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substituting new art for art of record would amount to rebutting a finding that the feature is not taught by any art in existence, which is not contemplated in reexamination (no comprehensive validity search). New art may rebut an examiner’s interpretation/finding of what the art of record shows, but not replace requester’s originally advanced art as a post-hoc substitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: New proposed rejection requirements in comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any newly proposed rejection based on newly presented prior art with third party comments must meet the guidelines of MPEP §2617.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a new proposed rejection stands on the same footing as a proposed rejection presented with the request for reexamination and must include the required discussion of the pertinency of each reference to the patentability of at least one claim and an explanation under 35 U.S.C. 311 of how the art is applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling improper third-party comments and rectification opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: If comments are directed to matters outside the Office action or patent owner response, or prior art submitted does not satisfy the (A)-(C) conditions, the written comments are improper and should be returned with an explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If already scanned into the Image File Wrapper, they should be expunged with notification to requester, providing 15 days to rectify and refile. Replacement comments must be strictly limited to the comments in the original returned submission; no additions beyond the original are allowed. If second submission remains improper, comments are returned and cannot be resubmitted for that response. This 15-day remedial opportunity is limited and does not apply to late or inappropriate comments under 37 CFR 1.957(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on supplemental third-party papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The third party requester is not permitted to file further papers to supplement the third party requester’s written comments (improper supplements will not be considered and will be returned).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A third party requester may, however, file written comments to any supplemental response filed by the patent owner. See MPEP §2666.20 for electing not to file comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of papers requirement (37 CFR 1.903)
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing a request for inter partes reexamination, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third party requester must be served on every other party in the reexamination proceeding in the manner provided in 37 CFR 1.248.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As proof of service, attach a certificate of service to the paper indicating the name and address of the party served and the method of service. A copy of the certificate must be attached with the copy of the paper served on the other party. Failure to reflect service may result in the document being refused consideration and will prompt a Notice of Defective Paper (PTOL-2069) with one month or 30 days (whichever is longer) to complete the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy when service is not made or proof missing
rubrics_metrics.description: If proof of service is not attached to a paper, a Notice of Defective Paper (PTOL-2069) will be mailed giving one month (or 30 days, whichever is longer) to supply service information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 26.68 (Lack of Service) may be used. If known that service was not made, use form paragraph 26.68 to give notice to the submitting party of the service requirement under 37 CFR 1.903. See MPEP §2620 for service of the initial request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness adjustment for late actual receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent owner’s response served on a third party requester is received by the requester more than 5 business days after the date of service on the certificate, the requester may submit a verified statement specifying the date of actual receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon submission of the verified statement specifying actual receipt date, the date of service will be deemed by the Office to be the date of actual receipt for the purpose of the third party’s 30-day comment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences when patent owner fails to respond (37 CFR 1.957)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner fails to file a timely, appropriate or complete response in an inter partes reexamination, prosecution may be terminated or limited depending on whether any claims were found patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (A) If no claims are found patentable, prosecution will be terminated and the Director will issue and publish a certificate concluding reexamination under §1.997 (NIRC). (B) If at least one claim is found patentable, further prosecution will be limited to the claim(s) found patentable at that time and to any claims added thereafter which do not expand the scope of those patentable claims; claims under rejection/objection may be withdrawn and canceled upon publication of the certificate. The ACP will set periods for patent owner response and third party comments under 37 CFR 1.951.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action Closing Prosecution (ACP) response rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A response to an ACP is not required; failure to respond to an ACP does not trigger the termination/limitation consequences of 37 CFR 1.957(b) and (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the patent owner does not respond to an ACP, the Office will issue a Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) in due course; different consequences apply than for ordinary failure to timely respond to an Office action prior to ACP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) and appeal consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patent owner fails to take timely appeal actions after issuance of a RAN, or where appeal is dismissed, consequences vary with whether claims were found patentable at time of failure to act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no claim found patentable at failure, NIRC issued. If at least one claim was found patentable and third party requester does not appeal or fails to continue appeal, prosecution should be terminated (NIRC). If third party appellant continues appeal, prosecution is limited to claims found patentable at time of failure to act. Third party may appeal withdrawal of a rejection stated in RAN as a final decision favorable to patentability (see 37 CFR 41.61(a)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Third party failure to timely comment on a patent owner response
rubrics_metrics.description: If a third party requester does not timely file written comments on a patent owner response, any subsequent submission of comments on that response will be refused consideration; the loss of commenting right applies only to that specific response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner’s response was incomplete and later completed, the third party may file comments on the completed response. However, where completion required only payment of a fee (other than an excess claims fee to support an amendment), the requester may not file comments after fee submission. Failure to timely appeal causes loss of appellate rights as appellant, though the requester may still act as respondent or enter the appeal under certain rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner withdrawal of a ground of rejection — general guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner withdraws a ground of rejection at any time in the prosecution of the inter partes reexamination, distinct treatments depend on origin of rejection and whether claims were amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (A) Where rejected originally by examiner, withdraw should be clearly stated as decision favorable to patentability; third party’s next comments may propose the withdrawn rejection as a 'rejection proposed by the third party requester' and may appeal withdrawal in RAN. (B) Where rejection was proposed by third party and claims not amended, treat issue as a rejection proposed by third party that examiner refuses to adopt. (C) Generally where claims amended and examiner withdraws a ground previously proposed by third party, this is not a refusal to adopt (rejection never proposed as to amended claims); third party may re-propose the rejection as to amended claims and may appeal if RAN issued. (D) If claim amended by adding a dependent claim previously subjected to a proposed requester rejection and the examiner withdraws that rejection as to the amended claim, treat as a refusal to adopt the requester’s previously proposed rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-fully responsive patent owner submissions (37 CFR 1.957(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: When a bona fide attempt to respond omits some matter necessary to a full response, the examiner may either waive deficiencies or treat the submission as incomplete and notify the patent owner to complete the response within a set period to avoid termination or limitation of prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Option (A): Waive minor deficiencies (e.g., fails to treat every rejection) and act on the submission; issue new Office action identifying remaining matters. Option (B): Treat as incomplete response and notify completion required within the period for response (or extension under 1.956) to avoid termination under 1.957(b) or limitation under 1.957(c). A serious deficiency (e.g., submission not filed in response to the Office action) would not be appropriate for waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art citation storage practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art citation proper under 37 CFR 1.501 submitted as a separate paper without argument will not be returned but stored until the ongoing reexamination is concluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior art returned by the examiner in connection with third party comments may be resubmitted as a separate prior art citation under 37 CFR 1.501 and will be stored until conclusion of the reexamination proceeding. See MPEP §§2204, 2206.
